definition: A particle emitter's Speed property should never be set to a literal zero when the emitter uses an orientation mode such as VelocityPerpendicular, because a zero velocity vector leaves the orientation calculation undefined and the particle clips out of existence entirely; setting Speed to a tiny nonzero value (the presenter's convention: 0.001) keeps the particle visually stationary while avoiding the degenerate zero-velocity case.
purpose: Achieve an effectively-stationary particle (no visible drift) without triggering a rendering failure that a literal zero value causes under velocity-dependent orientation modes.
visible_effect: At Speed = 0 with an affected orientation mode, the particle is invisible/clipped entirely; at Speed = 0.001, the particle is visually indistinguishable from stationary but renders normally.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Not applicable — a rendering-correctness workaround, not a perceptual/stylistic choice.
use_cases: any particle meant to stay effectively in place, on an emitter using a velocity-dependent orientation mode (VelocityParallel/VelocityPerpendicular)
non_use_cases: an emitter using an orientation mode that does not depend on velocity (FaceCamera, FaceCameraWorldUp), where a literal zero speed is not reported as causing this problem
cadence_representation: Not applicable — VFXSpec does not expose a raw Speed field for a caller to set to zero in the first place (it is subsumed into the chosen `primitive`/`scale`), so this exact degenerate case cannot be produced through `compile_effect`'s own surface. If Cadence ever exposes per-particle velocity directly, this is a concrete edge case worth guarding against at that time.
control_surface: None — outside VFXSpec's current field set.
failure_modes: setting Speed to exactly 0 on an emitter using a velocity-dependent orientation mode, causing the particle to clip out of existence rather than simply hold still
roblox_considerations: Specific to Roblox's ParticleEmitter Speed property interacting with its Orientation modes ("a lot of the time if you have face perpendicular, I think it just clips out of existence"); the presenter is not fully certain of the exact mechanism either, only the reliable workaround.
examples: "Speed, that's how fast it comes out. You can crank it up. You can set to zero. I would not set it to zero because a lot of the time if you have face perpendicular, I think it just clips out of existence... So, I always set it to 0.001 cuz it still doesn't move, but it stays there. So, never put that to zero" (video @ 03:45–04:08)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/u2o-wHKDlpw @ 03:45–04:08 — Twist states the workaround as a firm personal rule, while noting he is not fully certain of the underlying cause; experimental until validated
